analysis.title: International Market Intelligence | Morning Briefing (October 13, 2026)
key_insights: Overnight session was quiet with the US holiday, but the tape broadened while tech weakened. The tech selloff is extending with key technicals broken: SOX broke its 100-day moving average and KOSPI its 200-day.
EU earnings are off to a weak start (LVMH hit on China weakness). US banks begin Q3 reporting today and are the catalyst needed for the broadening trade to extend.

Signs of rising competition against AI oligopolies are weighing on the AI trade: MSFT's Maia chip becoming its primary inference system, NVDA in talks to acquire Reflection AI (US open-weight model developer), and China's CXMT reporting key progress on a new memory product.

Semis were the most net sold industry by hedge funds last week in North America (-1.5z), EMEA (-3z) and Japan, but remain a top-2 net exposure industry in every region. Broader tech positioning is less stretched than this summer, and AI infrastructure need not fall if broadening returns.

Gokul's US/UK marketing feedback on Asia Tech showed mixed sentiment. Concerns: rising share of open-source LLMs challenging ARR for proprietary models, how ROIC evolves at the model layer, and sustainability of funding for hyperscalers and neoclouds.
Q3 earnings preview: median Q3 y/y EPS growth is 8% for SPX and 9% for SXXP. The EU broadening trade has yet to come back and EU positioning vs US looks stretched.

Investors are constructive on earnings but worry results may underwhelm. JPM believes earnings will support the market and that consensus is not elevated, since global PMIs have accelerated to multi-year highs.

Semis earnings preview: constructive but selective on semis and semicap equipment. Fundamentals improved over three months on sustained AI infrastructure investment, supply tightness across the semis chain, and a cyclical recovery in non-AI end markets. Focus this quarter is on supply constraints (leading-edge foundry, memory) and when capacity can ease them.

Europe's political shift to the right is gaining traction (FT piece cited). France's budget debate starts today, and the key watch item is whether article 49.3 is triggered, which can lead to a no-confidence vote.
The EGB desk sees French OATs 25-30bps cheap vs fundamentals and other countries, but would not enter longs given the political backdrop.

Spain accounted for roughly a quarter of euro area growth (ex Ireland) in 1H26. The labour market is the clearest support, and strong job creation should support another solid quarter of private consumption.

Japan banks: retail JGBs are attracting attention after an August 2026 Nikkei article on possible tax benefits. If households buy them, funds likely come from bank deposits, which could worsen deposit competition. Megabanks with relatively low domestic loan-to-deposit ratios are better placed.

Tactically bullish on global equities. Regional preference is long US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) vs EU. The US is overheating, Europe is recovering from stagflation, and Asia has pockets of both.
The broadening trade can come back more clearly in the US than the EU. EU earnings fundamentals are good and positioning gives a buy signal, but EGB spreads need to stabilize for conviction in EU.

Longs: tech and supercycle themes (inference, semicap, less-levered hyperscalers, AI-vulnerables including application software), cyclicals with secular tailwinds (EU and JA banks, EU industrials, JA machinery, GE Infra, EU miners), low vol (EU pharma, UKX), and selectively consumer.
Shorts: AI-vulnerable (ex-software), short-cycle data center capex names, EU insurance, challenged industries (autos, chemicals, Asian consumer electronics, medtech) and MDAX.
Option hedges: keep MCX < UKX until clarity on spending, pragmatism and ideology; keep short France vs EU domestics on politics and dislocation.

Bullish on EM: since the end-July bottom EM has recovered over 9% of the drawdown but remains off YTD highs. Supports: global macro strength, AI capex tailwinds, commodity-driven broadening, scope for policy easing, political catalysts. Country-relative trades are preferred.

EM trades: tactically long China Star 50 vs KWEB, tactically long Korea vs South East Asia, tactically long Taiwan after the July global tech selloff (less volatile AI exposure than Korea). Hedges: long Brazil (EWZ) ahead of the end-of-month presidential runoff, and long EM (EEM) for broadening exposure.

HF positioning weekly wrap: performance is challenging (-0.8% MTD in October), equity L/S is the laggard (-1.2% globally), and EU managers are hit hardest (-1.3% MTD), with EU banks a detractor via negative crowding returns.

HF flows were flat with turnover about 0.5z below average. US net flows are increasingly correlated with market direction, so HFs could amplify moves. Retail sentiment is low while ETF flows are rebounding and seasonality favors positive ETF flows.
US positioning is steady (TPM about 46th percentile) while EU positioning fell to about the 13th percentile after -1.7z net selling, making the EU vs US gap look stretched.

HFs bought US banks a second week (just over +2z) ahead of earnings: large caps +1.5z over 5 days with positioning near highs, regionals sold (-0.9z). EU banks were modestly bought (<+1z) but positioning is elevated (+3z vs long-term), a key risk if Europe de-risks further.

Other sector flows: semis de-risked everywhere except AxJ (+1z buying), utilities remain near historically low HF positioning while ETF flows turned positive, and biotech remains weak but paused de-grossing.
